reason: The hypothesis relies on stress-induced segregation and brittle precipitate formation in a single-phase HEA, but the cited evidence (E1) describes thermal-aging-induced segregation driven by trace interstitials in a refractory HEA, not stress-driven segregation in a single-phase solid solution, and (E2) describes spontaneous phase separation in an as-cast dual-phase HEA wire, not deformation-induced precipitation in an initially homogeneous alloy. Neither passage supports the key mechanistic premises.
premises: High mechanical stress promotes local atomic diffusion and rearrangement in single-phase HEAs
Stress-driven segregation leads to nucleation of brittle, ordered precipitates at dislocation pile-ups and grain boundaries
These precipitates disrupt plastic flow and act as crack initiation sites, reducing toughness
The brittle transformation occurs only above a material-specific load/strain-rate threshold
The initial single-phase HEA is homogeneous and ductile with dimpled fracture
